# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0001 — in-body schema normalization + payment auto-balance + baggage recompute across 4 write tools
- Changes I made (1 line per edit):
  - book_reservation.py (clusters A+B): normalize passenger `date_of_birth`→`dob` and payment `{type,id}`→`{payment_id}`, coerce amount→int; on env "does not add up" error with exactly one credit card, rebalance credit=total−others and retry once.
  - update_reservation_passengers.py (A+D): normalize `date_of_birth`→`dob`; docstring now states the dob is in get_reservation_details so the agent need not ask the user / transfer.
  - update_reservation_flights.py (A): unwrap `payment_id` if the model passed a dict/list wrapper; plain string unchanged.
  - update_reservation_baggages.py (C): recompute nonfree_baggages from the policy free-allowance formula (free = table[membership][cabin]×num_pax), reading the reservation+user itself; overrides only when fully resolvable.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - A is the dominant SYSTEMIC cluster — gpt-oss-120b sends `date_of_birth`/`{type,id}` on nearly every write, pydantic rejects, turns burn. Normalization is a strict no-op on correct args (verified task 8 final call books first try, tasks 11/37 plain payment_id unchanged), so BOUNDED: only already-failing malformed inputs change.
  - B flips task 25 (verified: books with gold gift128/credit247=375). Fires only on the exact "does not add up" error with a single credit card.
  - C: no passing task calls update_reservation_baggages (0 in 8/11/37) → zero blast radius; corrects 22/17/12 within-free-allowance miscompute (verified gold/economy/2pax→0).
  - D is additive knowledge; cannot flip a passing decision.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — seed is the only prior (LEDGER baseline-only, RUNMAP empty, rejected.jsonl empty). Nothing to avoid re-trying yet.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: task 19 (transfer-vs-cancel; needs a discriminating cancellation-eligibility predicate — NOT a global rule loosen, which would regress task 37's legitimate flown-reservation transfer); task 23 (cancel + 3 certificate-split bookings); task 12 (business-upgrade pricing confusion); task 22 wrong-reservation disambiguation. Designs not yet tried: a cancellation-eligibility guard in cancel_reservation that reads booking time / insurance / cabin / flown-status and only blocks when none of the policy conditions hold.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). Lever used: in-body code guards (strongest for BEHAVIORAL schema/compute misses) + one knowledge docstring.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency not a declared objective here (reward is DB+COMMUNICATE only); but schema normalization also removes the 2–6 wasted retry turns the agent spends re-formatting every write, a latent efficiency win.
- Focus next iteration: a bounded cancellation-eligibility predicate guard in cancel_reservation (for task 19) and a composite upgrade/rebook flow; measure whether A alone cleared 25/22/17 before adding risk.
